```{r library-install}
library(torch)
library(torchvision)
library(ggplot2)

df_train <- read.csv("data_train.csv")
df_test <- read.csv("data_test.csv")
head(df_train)
```


```{r display-image}
# write a function that will display the image
plot_img <- function(x, im_shape = c(6, 6)) {
  # need to convert matrix to data frame for ggplot
  df <- data.frame(expand.grid(x = 1:im_shape[2], y = 1:im_shape[1]),
                   value = as.vector(t(x)))
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
    geom_tile() +
    # can choose how to map the 0 and 1 (I'm copying cmap from python here)
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "black", high = "white") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    scale_y_reverse()
}
```


```{r train-test-split}
x_train <- (df_train[,!names(df_train) %in% c("language")])
y_train <- df_train$language
x_test <- df_test[,!names(df_test) %in% c("language")]
y_test <- df_test$language

x_train <- as.matrix(x_train) / 255
x_test <- as.matrix(x_test) / 255


x_train <- torch_tensor(array(x_train, dim = c(dim(x_train)[1], 1, 32, 32)), dtype = torch_float())
x_test <- torch_tensor(array(x_test, dim = c(dim(x_test)[1], 1, 32, 32)), dtype = torch_float())
```


```{r image-transpose}
# images need to be transposed as all are sideways
plot_img(t(as.matrix(x_test[nrow(x_test),1,,])), im_shape = c(32, 32))
```

```{r cnn-model-train}
cnn_model <- nn_module(
  initialize = function() {
    # the channels are both 1 because we have black and white images (single matrix for each image)
    # this is the convolutional layer
    self$conv1 <- nn_conv2d(in_channels = 32, out_channels = 64, kernel_size = 3, stride = 1, padding=1)
    # pooling layer
    self$pool1 <- nn_max_pool2d(kernel_size = 2)
    # this is the convolutional layer
    self$conv2 <- nn_conv2d(in_channels = 64, out_channels = 128, kernel_size = 3, stride = 1)
    # pooling layer
    self$pool2 <- nn_max_pool2d(kernel_size = 2)
    # this is the hidden layer (I'm also speeding up things by making the network less wide)
    self$hid <- nn_linear(in_features = 4*4*128, out_features = 526) 
    
    # self$hid2 <- nn_linear(in_features = 250, out_features = 100)
    # this is the output layer
    self$out <- nn_linear(in_features = 526, out_features = 1)
  },
  # we're just going to call the data x which will be passed through each layer:
  forward = function(x) {
    x <- self$conv1(x)
    x <- self$pool1(x)
     x <- self$conv2(x)
    x <- self$pool2(x)
    x <- torch_flatten(x, start_dim = 2) # Flatten except for channel dimension
    x <- self$hid(x)
    x <- torch_relu(x)
    #x <- self$hid2(x)
    #x <- torch_tanh(x)
    x <- self$out(x)
    torch_sigmoid(x)
  }
)
```

```{r}
# initialize the model
model <- cnn_model()

# define the loss function and optimizer
loss_fn <- nn_bce_loss() # Binary Cross-Entropy (log-loss equivalent)
optimizer <- optim_sgd(model$parameters, lr = 0.2) #SGD (stochastic gradient descent)

epochs <- 10
n <- dim(x_train)[1]

# loop through the epochs manually
# (I think keras is a lot better here... I had to manually write out the updates that keras would)
# another way to speed it up is to implement a batch size, though the larger the batch size, the worse the fit tends to be
batch_size <- 32

for (epoch in seq_len(epochs)) {
  model$train()
  epoch_loss <- 0
  
  #  for (i in seq_len(n)) { #if not using batch size (will take MUCH longer)
  for (i in seq(1, n, by = batch_size)) {
    start <- i # only if using batch_size, comment out to do full training set
    end <- min(i + batch_size - 1, n) # only if using batch_size, comment out to do full training set
    
    # inputs <-x_train[i,,,drop = FALSE] #if not using batch size (will take MUCH longer)
    # output <- y_6train[i, drop = FALSE] #if not using batch size (will take MUCH longer)
    inputs <- x_train[start:end,,,]
    output <- y_train[start:end]
    
    # forward pass
    preds <- model(inputs)
    loss <- loss_fn(preds, output)
    
    # backprop
    optimizer$zero_grad()
    loss$backward()
    optimizer$step()
    
    epoch_loss <- epoch_loss + loss$item()
  }
  
  # cat(sprintf("Epoch %d, Loss: %.4f\n", epoch, epoch_loss / n)) #if not using batch size (will take MUCH longer)
  cat(sprintf("Epoch %d, Loss: %.4f\n", epoch, epoch_loss / (n / batch_size)))
}
```
